subject: Configural model for longitudinal model with dichotomous data

messages.author: 189d19347ab44a74
messages.subject: Configural model for longitudinal model with dichotomous data
parts:
Hi,

I am trying to adapt Millsap & Yun-Tein (2004) and Liu et al. (2017)'s categorical invariance cross-sectional and longitudinal models to my dichotomous longitudinal data. I have adapted a script from Sunthud based on Liu et al.'s paper.   

I am wondering if someone can confirm that I have specified the correct configural model below? 

I ask because when I run the model below I get that the model has not converged. However, when I restrict the factor loadings to be identical across time, the model converges, and when I add the additional constrain that the residual variances are all equal to 1, then the model also converges, and model fit does not degrade suggesting loading, threshold, and variance invariance. 

So, I am wondering if I'm setting up my configural model incorrectly or why it might not converge. I can generate data from my data set to replicate my error to share if my code is correct.

Thanks,
Chris 

configural.mod <- "

# define the factor models
# Note, the *.1 refers to Time 1, *.2 to Time 2, and *.3 to time 3.
fac2.1 =~ 1 * q1.1 + q4.1 + q10.1 + q11.1 + q19.1 + q23.1 + q27.1 + q28.1 + q15.1
fac2.2 =~ 1 * q1.2 + q4.2 + q10.2 + q11.2 + q19.2 + q23.2 + q27.2 + q28.2 + q15.2
fac2.3 =~ 1 * q1.3 + q4.3 + q10.3 + q11.3 + q19.3 + q23.3 + q27.3 + q28.3 + q15.3

# latent common factor variances and covariances
fac2.1 ~~ fac2.1 + fac2.2 + fac2.3
fac2.2 ~~ fac2.2 + fac2.3
fac2.3 ~~ fac2.3

# latent common factor means
fac2.1 ~ 0
fac2.2 ~ 1
fac2.3 ~ 1

# thresholds, restrict threshold to be constant across time
q1.1 | tau11 * t1
q4.1 | tau21 * t1
q10.1 | tau31 * t1
q11.1 | tau41 * t1
q19.1 | tau51 * t1
q23.1 | tau61 * t1
q27.1 | tau71 * t1
q28.1 | tau81 * t1
q15.1 | tau91 * t1

q1.2 | tau11 * t1
q4.2 | tau21 * t1
q10.2 | tau31 * t1
q11.2 | tau41 * t1
q19.2 | tau51 * t1
q23.2 | tau61 * t1
q27.2 | tau71 * t1
q28.2 | tau81 * t1
q15.2 | tau91 * t1

q1.3 | tau11 * t1
q4.3 | tau21 * t1
q10.3 | tau31 * t1
q11.3 | tau41 * t1
q19.3 | tau51 * t1
q23.3 | tau61 * t1
q27.3 | tau71 * t1
q28.3 | tau81 * t1
q15.3 | tau91 * t1

# residual covariances
q1.1 ~~ q1.2 + q1.3
q1.2 ~~ q1.3
q4.1 ~~ q4.2 + q4.3
q4.2 ~~ q4.3
q10.1 ~~ q10.2 + q10.3
q10.2 ~~ q10.3
q11.1 ~~ q11.2 + q11.3
q11.2 ~~ q11.3
q19.1 ~~ q19.2 + q19.3
q19.2 ~~ q19.3
q23.1 ~~ q23.2 + q23.3
q23.2 ~~ q23.3
q27.1 ~~ q27.2 + q27.3
q27.2 ~~ q27.3
q28.1 ~~ q28.2 + q28.3
q28.2 ~~ q28.3
q15.1 ~~ q15.2 + q15.3
q15.2 ~~ q15.3

# residuals
# fix for Time 1
q1.1 ~~ 1 * q1.1
q4.1 ~~ 1 * q4.1
q10.1 ~~ 1 * q10.1
q11.1 ~~ 1 * q11.1
q15.1 ~~ 1 * q15.1
q19.1 ~~ 1 * q19.1
q23.1 ~~ 1 * q23.1
q27.1 ~~ 1 * q27.1
q28.1 ~~ 1 * q28.1

# force to be estimated for Times 2 & 3
q1.2 ~~ NA * q1.2
q4.2 ~~ NA * q4.2
q10.2 ~~ NA * q10.2
q11.2 ~~ NA * q11.2
q15.2 ~~ NA * q15.2
q19.2 ~~ NA * q19.2
q23.2 ~~ NA * q23.2
q27.2 ~~ NA * q27.2
q28.2 ~~ NA * q28.2

q1.3 ~~ NA * q1.3
q4.3 ~~ NA * q4.3
q10.3 ~~ NA * q10.3
q11.3 ~~ NA * q11.3
q15.3 ~~ NA * q15.3
q19.3 ~~ NA * q19.3
q23.3 ~~ NA * q23.3
q27.3 ~~ NA * q27.3
q28.3 ~~ NA * q28.3

# fix all intercepts to 0
q1.1 + q4.1 + q10.1 + q11.1 + q15.1 + q19.1 + q23.1 + q27.1 + q28.1 ~ 0
q1.2 + q4.2 + q10.2 + q11.2 + q15.2 + q19.2 + q23.2 + q27.2 + q28.2 ~ 0
q1.3 + q4.3 + q10.3 + q11.3 + q15.3 + q19.3 + q23.3 + q27.3 + q28.3 ~ 0
"

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Configural model for longitudinal model with dichotomous data
parts:
I agree with Felix that you should read Wu & Estabrook and follow their advice.  Millsap & Tein were not exploring the issue fully.  The goal of that dissertation project was merely to identify the model in ONE such a way (not all possible ways) that no latent means or variances needed to be constrained to equality across groups in the configural model.  But that is not remotely necessary as a criterion, as long as you are aware of what identification constraints should be released because they are not necessary once certain equality constraints are imposed.  

Analogously, it is not necessary to use a marker variable with multivariate normal indicators.  You can fix the factor variances to 1 in the configural model for identification, as long as you remember to free all but one factor variance once you equate loadings.  The situation is simply more complicated with categorical indicators because the location/scale not only of latent common factors but also of latent item responses needs to be identified with constraints.  Millsap & Tein tried to simplify the issue by specifying a configural that required researchers to do nothing except add equality constraints to test invariance, but that simplification requires a complicated configural model that is statistically equivalent to the software defaults in Mplus and lavaan.  Wu & Estabrook (link below) explored the issue more completely, and in my opinion provide improved advice based on their more complete consideration of which measurement parameters can(not) be independently identified.  For example, Millsap & Tein simply ignored the issue of intercepts by assuming those were invariant.  But in Likert data (not binary, like yours) they can be separately identified from thresholds.  So it makes sense to test threshold equivalence before testing equivalence of loadings, intercepts, and residuals in the usual order we would follow with continuous data.  But with your binary data, testing equivalence of any type of measurement parameter requires assuming that the other three types are equivalent.

Anyway, the Millsap & Tein specification has trouble converging in R's optimizer that lavaan uses to estimate parameters, so if you can't get your model to run, that is another practical reason to consider using a different configural model that Millsap and Tein's.  But I do provide notes below to correct a few mistakes in your specification:
fac2.1 =~ 1 * q1.1

I think lavaanify() strips all whitespace anyway, but for clarity of reading, I would not leave space between your modifier and the variable.  

fac2.1 =~ 1*q1.1

# latent common factor means
fac2.1 ~ 0

To fix it to zero, this should be fac2.1 ~ 0*1

Think of "1" as the variable (actually the contant) on which fac2.1 is regressed, which provides estimation of the intercept (which is the grand mean when there are no other predictors).
# thresholds, restrict threshold to be constant across time

Correct

# residual covariances

Correct

# residuals
# fix for Time 1

# force to be estimated for Times 2 & 3
q1.2 ~~ NA * q1.2

Correct, BUT you need to fix the marker variable's variance to 1.
q1.2 ~~ 1*q1.2
q1.3 ~~ 1*q1.3
# fix all intercepts to 0

Correct, but this will be automatically the case, so you don't need it in the syntax.  If you do, then just as for the latent means, you need to say what parameter is fixed to zero by putting 0 as a modifier to the ~1 parameter:

q1.1 + q4.1 + q10.1 + q11.1 + q15.1 + q19.1 + q23.1 + q27.1 + q28.1 ~ 0*1
q1.2 + q4.2 + q10.2 + q11.2 + q15.2 + q19.2 + q23.2 + q27.2 + q28.2 ~ 0*1
q1.3 + q4.3 + q10.3 + q11.3 + q15.3 + q19.3 + q23.3 + q27.3 + q28.3 ~ 0*1

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
UvA web page: http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen
